sources.title: Resumable upload protocol 1.0.x
sources.locator: Protocol version/date lines 34-39; HEAD/PATCH example lines 57-99; offset mismatch and acknowledgement lines 135-145; OPTIONS and extension advertisement lines 146-172; creation lines 170-218; expiration lines 246-276; checksum lines 277-297; termination lines 327-336; concatenation lines 350-368.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary protocol page directly and read the normative core and extension sections, including the surrounding rules for offset, optional behavior, expiry, per-request checksums, termination, and concatenation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Core protocol requires HEAD to return the current Upload-Offset; PATCH offset mismatch requires 409 without changing the resource; success returns the new offset. Creation, expiration, checksum, termination, and concatenation are extensions discovered through OPTIONS/Tus-Extension. Expiration is optional; expired removed resources may return 404 or 410. Checksum validates a PATCH body, not automatically the assembled object. Termination SHOULD free associated resources.
sources.applicability: Direct basis for the Tus-facing option only. URL format, authentication, persistence, idempotent creation, whole-object verification, and backend storage are implementation choices.

sources.title: Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic version or publication date displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Multipart flow, same-number replacement, and ETag lines 23-41; ListParts pagination, unfinished-request omission, and completion-manifest warning lines 51-57; checksum types and consecutive-number rule lines 59-70 and 168-176; in-flight part behavior after stop lines 35-36; cleanup/cost lines 83-91; API permissions and KMS/SSE-C checksum conditions lines 144-166.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official AWS multipart overview and independently reopened its surrounding flow, listing, checksum table, encryption permission, and stop/abort sections to adjudicate C1 and C2.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS uses an upload ID and part number; reusing a part number replaces its former part; Complete needs the part-number/ETag list; a completed MPU ETag is not necessarily a whole-object MD5. ListParts returns at most 1,000 parts and excludes unfinished requests; AWS says maintain the specified part-number/ETag list for Complete. AWS full-object checksum types listed are CRC64NVME, CRC32, and CRC32C, while SHA-256 is listed as composite; with multipart checksums, part numbers must be consecutive from 1. KMS checksum use requires relevant KMS permissions, including decrypt; SSE-C Complete must include required headers for a returned checksum. In-flight parts can still succeed or fail after stop. AWS-only.
sources.applicability: Evidence only for Amazon S3. The unknown compatible service must be tested for part limits/order, listing and in-flight operation semantics, checksum type and encryption requirements, completion, abort, cleanup, and permissions. Do not treat AWS evidence as a compatibility guarantee.

sources.title: Amazon S3 multipart upload limits
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic version or publication date displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary AWS limits page directly and read its maximum object, part count, part number, part-size, last-part, and ListParts limits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS documents a 48.8 TiB maximum object, 10,000 parts, part numbers 1-10,000, parts 5 MiB-5 GiB with no minimum for the last part, and up to 1000 parts in one ListParts response.
sources.applicability: AWS limits only. The 16 MiB arithmetic in the proposal fits the stated file sizes under these AWS values; the compatible vendor remains unqualified.

sources.title: Aborting a multipart upload
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic version or publication date displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Object visibility before successful completion, incomplete-part billing, and lifecycle note lines 4-9; abort by upload ID and cleanup guidance lines 73-84.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official AWS abort page directly and read its object visibility, incomplete-part cost, lifecycle, and upload-ID abort rules. In-flight request behavior is separately recorded from S2.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For AWS, an object is created only when CompleteMultipartUpload succeeds; uploaded parts remain billable until complete or abort; lifecycle configuration can stop incomplete uploads; aborting by upload ID prevents further new part uploads using that ID. S2 separately documents that already in-flight calls can still finish after stop, so exact cleanup timing must account for them.
sources.applicability: Supports the AWS cleanup comparison only. It does not establish equivalent semantics for the fictional compatible vendor.

sources.title: Announcement: S3 default integrity change, aws-sdk-rust issue 1240
sources.publisher: AWS SDK for Rust maintainers, awslabs/aws-sdk-rust
sources.released_version_or_commit: AWS SDK for Rust S3 client v1.69.0; issue opened 2025-01-16; no issue commit used as release identity.
sources.locator: Issue Open status and maintainer description, lines 140-162.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the AWS SDK for Rust maintainers issue, checked the status and opening date, and read the v1.69.0 default-checksum and third-party compatibility statement.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The maintainer announcement says S3 clients from AWS SDK for Rust v1.69.0 add checksums by default on Put calls and validate Get calls. It warns that third-party implementations may not yet support newly enabled defaults. WHEN_REQUIRED configuration is mentioned as a way to disable the new behavior, but maintainers say they do not recommend disabling integrity protections.
sources.applicability: Relevant only if the gateway or another Rust component uses this AWS SDK against a compatible storage API. Supports exact endpoint/library qualification, not disabling integrity or assuming AWS-compatible semantics.

criticism_dispositions.finding: The critique is right that “verified” needs an explicit checksum algorithm and encryption/permission conditions. AWS documents CRC64NVME, CRC32, and CRC32C as full-object types and SHA-256 as composite, with KMS and SSE-C conditions for checksum availability. The final uses a matching strong full-object digest or authorized read-back SHA-256; it does not equate CRC or composite checksum with the source SHA-256 byte-match claim.
criticism_dispositions.remaining_uncertainty: The target provider and its exact checksum/encryption behavior are unknown.

criticism_dispositions.finding: The critique is right that an absent ListParts result does not show an unfinished request failed and same-number reupload can overwrite. AWS documents that in-flight parts may finish after stop. The final blocks retry/completion while the operation is Unknown, waits for resolution or retires the MPU ID, and queues cleanup.
criticism_dispositions.remaining_uncertainty: The exact compatible provider may differ; its request-settling, abort, and cleanup behavior must be tested.
